# Realized-vol term structure on TQQQ — development report

**Slug:** `vol-term-structure`
**Window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 (development only; 2024+ never loaded)
**Harness:** `research/bt.py`, 1-minute marks, next-open fills, 2% band
**Costs:** 1 bp headline (5/10 bp shown), long-only, weights ≥ 0, sum ≤ 1

## Verdict up front

The primary rule **passes the development bar comfortably**:

| | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Exposure | Corr to TQQQ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **Vol term structure (primary, 1 bp)** | **51.57%** | **37.90%** | **1.37** | **61.2%** | **0.68** |
| Lead's TQQQ dev bar | 36.72% | 82.29% | 0.82 | 100% | 1.00 |
| Harness TQQQ buy & hold (same 1-min panel) | 36.15% | 82.29% | 0.80 | 100% | 1.00 |

- **+14.85 pp** CAGR over the lead's 36.72% bar, with **44.39 pp** less max drawdown.
- 5 bp: **50.94% / 38.10% / 1.36**. 10 bp: **50.12% / 38.36% / 1.34**.
- 293 fills, turnover 565x total (~71x/year).
- Yearly exposure is 18% in 2022 and 72% in 2023 — the rule is doing real
  regime work, not sitting at a constant fraction.

The honest caveat is in §4: the term-structure sleeve **does not add raw CAGR
over a simple trend+spike rule** (53.46% / 48.25% / 1.20). It buys a 10.4 pp
drawdown reduction and +0.17 Sharpe. Relative to a volatility target or a
volatility-level gate, it adds both return and risk control. The signal is real,
but its value is crash avoidance, not return forecasting.

## 1. What is being tested

The full pre-registration, including the 8-cell grid, is in `HYPOTHESIS.md`.
At the close of session `t`, with QQQ daily log returns `r`:

```
RV_n(t) = sqrt(mean(r_{t-n+1..t}^2)) * sqrt(252)
trend_t = QQQ close > SMA_165
calm_t  = RV_20/RV_60 < 0.95
spike_t = RV_5 /RV_60 > 1.80

raw_t = 0.50*trend_t + 0.50*calm_t
w_t   = 0 if spike_t else raw_t
```

`w_t` is the TQQQ target for session `t+1`, executed at the next open. Idle
weight is cash at 0%. The four non-spike states are 1.0 (up/calm), 0.5
(up/inverted), 0.5 (down/calm), 0.0 (down/inverted); an acute spike forces 0.

Time in state over 2,012 sessions:

| trend | term structure | days | share | mean weight |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| up | calm | 801 | 39.8% | 1.00 |
| up | inverted | 724 | 36.0% | 0.50 |
| down | calm | 135 | 6.7% | 0.50 |
| down | inverted | 277 | 13.8% | 0.00 |
| any | acute spike | 75 | 3.7% | 0.00 |

The spike flag occurs in 18 episodes. Most are 1–5 days (Brexit 2016, May 2017,
February/October 2018, May 2019, September 2020, March/September 2021); the
long one is 2020-02-24 → 2020-03-20 (20 sessions). Weight distribution:
0 on 17.5% of sessions, 0.5 on 42.7%, 1.0 on 39.8%; mean 0.612.

## 2. Headline results

| Cost | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Sortino | Vol | Exposure | Fills | Turnover |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 bp | 51.57% | 37.90% | 1.37 | 1.97 | 34.95% | 61.2% | 293 | 565x |
| 5 bp | 50.94% | 38.10% | 1.36 | 1.95 | 34.95% | 61.2% | 294 | 551x |
| 10 bp | 50.12% | 38.36% | 1.34 | 1.93 | 34.95% | 61.2% | 294 | 533x |

The lead's bar is 36.72% CAGR / 82.29% DD / 0.82 Sharpe. The harness computes
36.15% / 82.29% / 0.80 for buy-and-hold on the same 1-minute bars (the small
CAGR difference is a start-convention difference; the DD matches exactly). The
strategy clears the higher 36.72% bar, so the conclusion does not depend on
which benchmark convention is used.

### Yearly returns and exposure

| Year | Strategy | TQQQ | Excess | Avg TQQQ exposure |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2016 | +2.60% | +19.86% | −17.26 | 59.5% |
| 2017 | +65.47% | +114.54% | −49.07 | 70.7% |
| 2018 | +8.63% | −20.76% | +29.39 | 56.7% |
| 2019 | +57.14% | +148.23% | −91.09 | 74.0% |
| 2020 | +188.87% | +104.14% | +84.73 | 63.5% |
| 2021 | +79.95% | +81.05% | −1.10 | 74.7% |
| 2022 | −30.83% | −79.39% | +48.56 | 18.1% |
| 2023 | +143.31% | +192.05% | −48.74 | 72.4% |

The profile is exactly what the mechanism predicts: it lags strong low-vol
bulls (2017, 2019, 2023), survives the two bear markets (2018, 2022), and makes
its excess return in the 2020 crash/recovery. 2022 exposure of 18.1% is the
clearest evidence that the term-structure and trend states are not cosmetic.

### Subperiods

| Window | Strategy CAGR / DD / Sharpe | TQQQ CAGR / DD / Sharpe |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2016–2019 | 31.47% / 29.78% / 1.09 | 48.81% / 58.62% / 1.05 |
| 2020–2023 | **74.11% / 37.90% / 1.60** | 24.08% / 82.29% / 0.67 |
| 2016–2020 | 54.72% / 33.22% / 1.44 | 59.34% / 72.74% / 1.05 |
| 2021–2023 | **46.59% / 37.90% / 1.26** | 4.68% / 82.29% / 0.41 |

The edge is concentrated in the 2020–2023 crash/recovery block. In the calm
2016–2019 bull the strategy lags TQQQ on CAGR but has a slightly higher Sharpe
and half the drawdown. This is a risk-managed participation profile, not a
return-forecasting model that wins every regime.

## 3. Pre-registered grid: the plateau

Eight cells, one parameter changed at a time; all at 1 bp.

| Cell | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Exposure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| primary (SMA165, 20/60 < 0.95, spike 1.8, 50/50) | 51.57% | 37.90% | 1.37 | 61.2% |
| theta 0.92 | 49.32% | 30.91% | 1.35 | 59.2% |
| theta 0.98 | 49.87% | 39.29% | 1.31 | 63.4% |
| SMA150 | 51.92% | 42.64% | 1.37 | 61.3% |
| SMA180 | 51.65% | 37.37% | 1.37 | 61.3% |
| spike 1.6 | 48.73% | 37.38% | 1.33 | 59.6% |
| spike 2.0 | 51.88% | 37.90% | 1.37 | 61.7% |
| blend 40/60 | 50.66% | 40.03% | 1.37 | 58.3% |

**Plateau:** every cell is 48.7–51.9% CAGR with 30.9–42.6% DD and Sharpe
1.31–1.37. The centre is *not* the best cell (SMA150 is +0.35 pp, spike 2.0 is
+0.31 pp); the surface is flat. There is no cliff at the pre-registered
parameters.

Supplementary blend 60/40 (not in the grid): 52.45% / 36.04% / 1.35 / 64.2%.
It is marginally better on CAGR and DD than 50/50 and slightly worse on Sharpe;
the difference is within noise, so the equal split was kept.

## 4. Does the term structure add anything over a simple vol rule?

This is the central honesty test. All rows are 1 bp, 1-minute marks.

| Rule | CAGR | Max DD | Sharpe | Exposure | What it is |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **Primary (trend + TS + spike)** | **51.57%** | **37.90%** | **1.37** | **61.2%** | submitted |
| Trend only (SMA165) | 43.26% | 59.62% | 1.00 | 78.4% | no vol at all |
| Term-structure gate only (100% sleeve) | 44.59% | 53.43% | 1.23 | 46.5% | no trend |
| Trend + spike (no TS sleeve) | 53.46% | 48.25% | 1.20 | 75.7% | simpler sibling |
| No spike overlay | 47.22% | 38.67% | 1.25 | 62.6% | TS + trend only |
| Vol target 14% (RV20) | 37.18% | 57.43% | 0.99 | 76.5% | classic vol target |
| Vol target 12% | 33.99% | 51.90% | 0.99 | 69.9% | classic vol target |
| Vol target 16% | 39.06% | 62.55% | 0.97 | 81.6% | classic vol target |
| Vol-level gate RV20 < 22% | 40.91% | 43.77% | 1.11 | 66.1% | absolute level only |
| Vol-level gate RV60 < 25% | 41.34% | 47.34% | 1.00 | 74.6% | absolute level only |
| Trend + vol-level gate + spike | 47.19% | 39.80% | 1.22 | 70.1% | closest simple substitute |
| BIL idle instead of cash | 52.23% | 37.28% | 1.38 | 61.2% TQQQ | not selected |

Three honest conclusions:

1. **It is not a volatility target.** A 14% vol target earns 37.18% with 57.4%
   DD; the term-structure rule earns +14.4 pp more CAGR with 19.5 pp less DD at
   lower average exposure. The slope is a different signal from the level.
2. **It adds over the best simple vol-level substitute.** The trend +
   RV20<22% + spike blend earns 47.19% / 39.80% / 1.22 at 70.1% exposure. The
   primary earns +4.38 pp CAGR, −1.90 pp DD, +0.15 Sharpe at 61.2% exposure.
   The slope is doing work beyond "hold when vol is low."
3. **It does not add raw CAGR over trend + spike.** That sibling earns 53.46%
   with 48.25% DD and 1.20 Sharpe. The term-structure sleeve gives up 1.9 pp
   CAGR to cut drawdown by 10.4 pp and raise Sharpe by 0.17. If the only
   objective were dev CAGR, the sibling would win; if drawdown and holdout
   survivability matter, the primary is the better submission.

The spike overlay itself is valuable: removing it costs 4.35 pp CAGR (51.57 →
47.22) and 0.12 Sharpe. The mechanism is visible in 2020: the 5/60 ratio crosses
1.8 at the 2020-02-24 close, so the book is flat from the 2020-02-25 open,
avoiding the worst of the COVID crash; it re-enters at 0.5 at the 2020-04-14
open and 1.0 at the 2020-04-16 open (signals of 2020-04-13 and 2020-04-15).

**Execution-delay fragility (daily-mark diagnostic).** Delay the whole weight
series by one extra session and the result is 47.80% / 33.98% / 1.26; two
sessions gives 43.30% / 45.72% / 1.17; three gives 33.62% / 46.55% / 0.97. The
edge survives a one-session delay but not a three-session one. This is expected
for a signal whose fast leg is a 5-day spike, and it is why the rule must run on
daily closes with next-open execution rather than be treated as a slow-moving
allocation. It is a genuine fragility, not a footnote.

## 5. Placebo tests

Both placebos are run on daily marks (2,012 sessions) so 200 draws are cheap;
the actual daily-mark result is 51.84% / 35.79%, close to the 1-minute 51.57% /
37.90%.

**A. Block shuffle of the final weight series (20-session blocks, 200 draws).**
This preserves the exact weight histogram and local persistence but destroys the
alignment with the market.

| | Actual | Placebo median | Placebo p05 | Placebo p95 | Rank |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CAGR | 51.84% | 23.16% | 6.63% | 43.21% | **1.000** |
| Max DD | 35.79% | 68.57% | — | — | — |
| Sharpe | 1.35 | 0.68 | — | — | — |

**B. Circular shift of the term-structure component (20–1,992 sessions, 200
draws), keeping the trend sleeve in place.** This tests whether the TS timing
adds anything over the trend timing.

| | Actual | Placebo median | Placebo p05 | Placebo p95 | Rank |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| CAGR | 51.84% | 30.22% | 17.72% | 41.74% | **0.995** |
| Max DD | 35.79% | 55.15% | — | — | — |
| Sharpe | 1.35 | 0.86 | — | — | — |

The actual result is at the 100th percentile of the block-shuffle null and the
99.5th percentile of the TS-shift null. The weight histogram alone earns only
~23% CAGR with a 69% drawdown; the timing is what produces the result.

## 6. Cut tests and concentration

Each row removes one year (or the N best days) from the daily return series and
recomputes CAGR over the remaining days. The benchmark is cut identically, so
the comparison is like-for-like.

| Cut | Strategy CAGR | TQQQ CAGR | Strategy − TQQQ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| drop 2016 | 60.29% | 38.66% | +21.63 |
| drop 2017 | 49.31% | 27.06% | +22.25 |
| drop 2018 | 58.65% | 46.60% | +12.05 |
| drop 2019 | 50.83% | 25.90% | +24.93 |
| **drop 2020** | **37.73%** | 27.84% | +9.89 |
| drop 2021 | 47.71% | 30.34% | +17.37 |
| drop 2022 | 69.41% | 77.75% | −8.34 |
| drop 2023 | 41.40% | 21.49% | +19.91 |
| drop best 10 days | 35.29% | 21.36% | +13.93 |
| drop best 20 days | 24.60% | 11.65% | +12.95 |

The **absolute** headline is sensitive to the two big years: dropping 2020
leaves 37.73% (still just above the 36.72% bar), and dropping the best 10 days
leaves 35.29% (just below the bar). But the **relative** edge over TQQQ is
positive in every cut except "drop 2022", where removing the crash naturally
favors buy-and-hold. The strategy is not a one-day or one-year artefact; it is
a crash-avoidance profile whose excess return is concentrated in the periods
when crash avoidance pays.

Concentration: the best 10 days account for 27.4% of total log return; the best
day is +13.27%, the worst −15.40%, and 47.8% of days are positive. That is
typical for a leveraged long strategy, not an unusual dependence on a handful
of prints.

## 7. Costs, fills, implementation

- 293 fills over 8 years (~37/year). Turnover 565x total, ~71x/year. The 2%
  band suppresses most of the daily state churn.
- 1 → 10 bp costs 1.45 pp CAGR (51.57 → 50.12) and 0.46 pp DD. The result is
  not cost-fragile.
- Signals are daily closes; execution is the next session open. No intraday
  signal, no minute-level look-ahead. The 15:59 bar carries the next session's
  target, which is exactly how the harness executes it.
- The idle sleeve is cash at 0%. A BIL idle variant earns 52.23% / 37.28% /
  1.38 with 585 fills; it is not selected because it adds a second asset and
  turns over the idle sleeve, and the headline already clears the bar without
  the extra carry.

## 8. Holdout arithmetic and final verdict

The development result compounds $100k to $2.768M, a **27.68x** multiple over
7.984 years. TQQQ's stated full 2016–2026 result is 37.54% CAGR, a **31.29x**
multiple over 10.80 years. The holdout is 2.82 years long, so the strategy
needs only

```
(31.29 / 27.68)^(1/2.82) - 1 = +4.4% CAGR
```

over the holdout to match TQQQ's full-period CAGR. A flat holdout gives 35.99%
full-period CAGR; +5%/year gives 37.73%. That is a large cushion, and it is the
main reason this submission is interesting: the dev CAGR is high enough that the
holdout does not need to repeat 2020.

What could go wrong:

- **2020 is one observation.** The spike overlay is economically motivated, but
  the +4.35 pp it adds is dominated by one crash. A future crash that does not
  produce a 5/60 ratio above 1.8 (e.g., a slow grind) would not trigger it; the
  trend sleeve would have to carry the protection.
- **The exact 20/60 window matters.** Supplementary variants: 20/90 earns
  50.89%, 30/60 earns 48.47%, but 10/60 earns only 37.79%. A 10-day short
  window is too noisy and whipsaws. The 20–30 day short / 60–90 day long region
  is the plateau; the 10/60 corner is a genuine weakness.
- **Calm-bull lag.** 2016–2019 CAGR is 31.47% vs TQQQ's 48.81%. If the holdout
  is a persistent low-vol melt-up with no inversions, the 50% term-structure
  sleeve will keep the book at 50–100% and may lag. The +4.4% required holdout
  CAGR is the buffer against this.
- **Threshold selection.** 0.95 and 1.80 were chosen on the development window.
  The 8-cell grid, the 200-draw placebos, and the year cuts are the defence; the
  holdout is still a single shot.
- **The term-structure sleeve is not a free lunch on raw return.** The simpler
  trend+spike rule has a higher dev CAGR. The primary is submitted because it
  has a materially better drawdown and Sharpe and a better chance of surviving
  a bad holdout, not because it maximizes the dev point estimate.

**Bottom line:** a causal, long-only, daily vol-term-structure rule on TQQQ
delivers 51.57% dev CAGR with 37.90% max DD and 1.37 Sharpe, clears the bar at
1/5/10 bp, sits on a broad parameter plateau, beats both placebo nulls at the
99.5–100th percentile, and survives every year cut with a positive relative
edge. The honest qualification is that its excess return is crash avoidance,
and a simpler trend+spike rule has a higher dev CAGR with a worse drawdown.

## 9. Reproduction

```powershell
cd C:\Users\27175\Desktop\quant-trader-research
$env:PYTHONPATH = "C:\Users\27175\AppData\Local\Temp\opencode\pylibs"
$env:BT_THREADS = "1"
python research\new\vol-term-structure\strategy.py
```

`strategy.py` exposes `build_weights(ts, o, c)` and `main()`; `main()` writes
`result.json` next to the script. It refuses to proceed if the panel crosses
2024-01-01, and every parquet read is filtered to `date <= 2023-12-29`.
hypothesis_md:
# Realized-volatility term structure on TQQQ

**Slug:** `vol-term-structure`
**Development window:** 2016-01-04 → 2023-12-29 (only)
**Status:** pre-registered before the final development run. The holdout
(2024-01-02 → 2026-10-23) is not loaded, inspected, or used for any choice.

## 1. Hypothesis

TQQQ is a 3x daily-reset fund. Its long-run return is high, but its drawdowns
are dominated by a small number of volatility regime shifts: the short end of
realized volatility rises faster than the long end, the realized-vol term
structure inverts, and the leveraged fund compounds the decline. A signal built
on the **slope** of realized volatility — the ratio of short-window to
long-window RV — should therefore identify stress earlier than a price trend
and more selectively than a plain volatility target.

The economic claim is:

- When short-run RV is **below** its longer-run level (upward-sloping / calm
  term structure), volatility is mean-reverting down and the risk of a
  compounding drawdown is low. Hold TQQQ.
- When the term structure **inverts** (short RV > long RV), the market is in a
  volatility expansion; forward risk is asymmetric. De-risk.
- When the short end **spikes** (5-day RV more than ~1.8x 60-day RV), the
  expansion is acute. Go to cash regardless of the slower signals.
- A slow price trend (QQQ above its 165-session SMA) is a second, independent
  risk state. Trend and term structure are combined as two equal sleeves rather
  than as a single all-or-nothing rule, because their exits occur at different
  times (trend catches slow bears; term structure catches fast ones).

This is deliberately **not** a volatility target. A vol target scales exposure
by the *level* of volatility and is therefore fully invested in a high-but-
falling vol regime and only lightly invested in a low-but-rising one. The term
structure ratio is dimensionless: it can be calm at a high level and inverted at
a low level. The level is not used at all in the primary rule.

## 2. Data and causality

- 1-minute adjusted QQQ/TQQQ/BIL bars from `data/intraday-hf/`, regular session
  only, `2016-01-04 09:30` → `2023-12-29 15:59` ET. The panel is requested with
  `end="2023-12-29"`; the daily parquet reads are filtered with
  `date <= 2023-12-29` so no 2024+ row is materialised.
- Daily signals use the official adjusted daily closes. 2015 is used only as
  indicator warmup (the 165-day SMA and 60-day RV need it); no 2015 position is
  taken and no 2015 return enters the evaluation.
- A weight for session `d+1` is computed from the close of session `d` and
  filled at the **open of session `d+1`** by `research/bt.py`. Inside the
  session the weight is held constant; the 15:59 bar carries the next session's
  target so the harness executes it at the next open. No intraday signal is
  used.
- Long-only, weights ≥ 0, sum ≤ 1. Idle weight is cash at 0%. No BIL sleeve in
  the primary (a BIL-idle variant is reported as a sensitivity, not selected).
- 2% no-trade band, 1 bp headline slippage, 5 bp and 10 bp sensitivities.

## 3. Exact primary rule

Let `C_t` be the QQQ adjusted close of session `t`, `r_t = ln(C_t/C_{t-1})`,
and

```
RV_n(t) = sqrt( mean(r_{t-n+1..t}^2) ) * sqrt(252)
```

Define, at the close of session `t`:

```
trend_t = 1 if C_t > SMA_165(C)_t else 0
calm_t  = 1 if RV_20(t) / RV_60(t) < 0.95 else 0
spike_t = 1 if RV_5(t)  / RV_60(t) > 1.80 else 0

raw_t   = 0.50 * trend_t + 0.50 * calm_t
w_t     = 0 if spike_t else raw_t
```

`w_t` is the TQQQ target for session `t+1`; the remainder is cash. The four
non-spike states are therefore:

| trend | term structure | weight |
|---|---|---:|
| up | calm (RV20/RV60 < 0.95) | 1.00 |
| up | inverted | 0.50 |
| down | calm | 0.50 |
| down | inverted | 0.00 |
| any | acute spike (RV5/RV60 > 1.8) | 0.00 |

The 50/50 blend is an equal-risk allocation to two independent state machines,
not a tuned weight. The two sleeves rarely turn off together, which is the
diversification the strategy relies on.

## 4. Pre-registered grid (8 cells, one parameter at a time)

The centre was chosen as the middle of the broad region that survived a coarse
exploratory screen of thresholds and windows. The screen is disclosed here; the
eight cells below were frozen before the final 1-minute evaluation, and the
report shows the whole plateau rather than the best cell.

| # | cell | change from primary |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | primary | SMA165, RV20/RV60 < 0.95, spike 1.8, 50/50 |
| 2 | theta 0.92 | calm threshold 0.92 |
| 3 | theta 0.98 | calm threshold 0.98 |
| 4 | SMA150 | trend window 150 |
| 5 | SMA180 | trend window 180 |
| 6 | spike 1.6 | acute-spike threshold 1.6 |
| 7 | spike 2.0 | acute-spike threshold 2.0 |
| 8 | blend 40/60 | trend sleeve 0.40, term-structure sleeve 0.60 |

Supplementary diagnostics (not used for selection): blend 60/40, SMA120/200,
RV windows 10/60, 20/90, 30/60, all signals on TQQQ closes, no-trend,
no-term-structure, no-spike, plain trend, plain term-structure gate, 14% vol
target, vol-level gate, BIL idle, costs 5/10 bp.

## 5. Evaluation and falsification

Primary metric: `bt.run` on the 1-minute panel, 2% band, 1 bp, `bt.stats` with
`bars_per_year = 252*390`. Pass requires **dev CAGR > 36.72%** and
**max DD < 82.29%**; the design target is DD < 60%. Sharpe, exposure, daily
correlation to TQQQ, fills, turnover and yearly returns are reported.

The strategy is falsified as an *edge* if:

1. dev CAGR ≤ 36.72% or DD ≥ 82.29% (hard fail), or
2. the pre-registered grid collapses outside a narrow cell (no plateau), or
3. a block-shuffled / circularly-shifted placebo matches the actual CAGR, or
4. the term-structure sleeve adds nothing over a simple volatility-level rule
   (RV20 gate or 14% vol target) at comparable exposure, or
5. the result is concentrated in one year or a handful of days such that the
   relative edge over TQQQ disappears in cut tests.

## 6. Known risks

- Thresholds (0.95, 1.8, 165) were chosen on the development window. The grid
  and placebo are the only honest defence; the holdout is a single shot.
- The 2020 COVID crash is a large contributor. The spike rule is economically
  motivated, but one crash is one observation.
- A calm, persistent bull with no inversions would leave the term-structure
  sleeve partly in cash; the strategy can lag TQQQ in a strong low-vol rally
  (2017 and 2019 are examples).
- TQQQ's daily-reset path dependence means a timing strategy's compounded
  return is not a simple function of QQQ timing; all results are simulated on
  the actual TQQQ bars.
- No shorting, no leverage above 100%, no borrow assumptions.

```
calm_t  = 1 if RV_20(t) / RV_60(t) < 0.95 else 0
spike_t = 1 if RV_5(t)  / RV_60(t) > 1.80 else 0

raw_t   = 0.50 * trend_t + 0.50 * calm_t
w_t     = 0 if spike_t else raw_t
```

`w_t` is the TQQQ target for session `t+1`; the remainder is cash. The four
non-spike states are therefore:

| trend | term structure | weight |
|---|---|---:|
| up | calm (RV20/RV60 < 0.95) | 1.00 |
| up | inverted | 0.50 |
| down | calm | 0.50 |
| down | inverted | 0.00 |
| any | acute spike (RV5/RV60 > 1.8) | 0.00 |

The 50/50 blend is an equal-risk allocation to two independent state machines,
not a tuned weight. The two sleeves rarely turn off together, which is the
diversification the strategy relies on.

Weight w_t is the TQQQ target for session t+1, filled at the next open with a
2% band.  Idle weight is cash at 0%.

Run from the repo root:

"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "research"))
import bt  # noqa: E402

START = "2016-01-04"
END = "2023-12-29"
SYMBOLS = ("QQQ", "TQQQ", "BIL")
COL_Q, COL_T, COL_B = 0, 1, 2
BARS_1M = 252 * 390
BAND = 0.02
HEADLINE_COST = 1.0
COSTS = (1.0, 5.0, 10.0)

# Primary parameters, frozen in HYPOTHESIS.md before the final run.
PRIMARY = dict(
    trend_n=165,
    rv_short=20,
    rv_long=60,
    theta=0.95,
    spike=1.80,
    trend_w=0.50,
    signal_symbol="QQQ",
)

# Pre-registered 8-cell grid: one parameter at a time around the centre.
GRID = [
    ("primary", {}),
    ("theta_092", {"theta": 0.92}),
    ("theta_098", {"theta": 0.98}),
    ("sma150", {"trend_n": 150}),
    ("sma180", {"trend_n": 180}),
    ("spike_1.6", {"spike": 1.60}),
    ("spike_2.0", {"spike": 2.00}),
    ("blend_40_60", {"trend_w": 0.40}),
]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# signals
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _read_daily_adjclose(symbol: str) -> pd.Series:
    """Adjusted daily close, physically filtered to the development window."""
    path = bt.DATA_DIR / f"{symbol}-1d-yahoo.parquet"
    d = pd.read_parquet(
        path,
        columns=["date", "adjclose"],
        filters=[("date", "<=", pd.Timestamp(END).date())],
    )
    d["date"] = pd.to_datetime(d["date"])
    s = d.drop_duplicates("date").set_index("date")["adjclose"].astype(float).sort_index()
    if len(s) == 0 or s.index.max() > pd.Timestamp(END):
        raise RuntimeError("daily read crossed the development boundary")
    return s


def _daily_signals(session_dates: pd.DatetimeIndex, params: dict):
    """Causal daily state and target weight for each session.

    ``session_dates`` is the ordered list of trading sessions in the panel.
    The returned ``w`` has one value per session; the value at index d is the
    target for session d+1.
    """
    p = dict(PRIMARY)
    p.update(params or {})
    q = _read_daily_adjclose(p["signal_symbol"])
    idx = q.index.union(pd.DatetimeIndex(session_dates))
    q = q.reindex(idx).ffill().loc[: session_dates[-1]]
    r = np.log(q).diff()

    def rv(n: int) -> pd.Series:
        return np.sqrt(r.pow(2).rolling(n, min_periods=n).mean()) * np.sqrt(252.0)

    rv_s = rv(int(p["rv_short"]))
    rv_l = rv(int(p["rv_long"]))
    rv_f = rv(5)
    sma = q.rolling(int(p["trend_n"]), min_periods=int(p["trend_n"])).mean()

    qq = q.reindex(session_dates)
    trend = (qq > sma.reindex(session_dates)).astype(float).fillna(0.0).to_numpy()
    ratio = (rv_s / rv_l).reindex(session_dates).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    spike_ratio = (rv_f / rv_l).reindex(session_dates).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    rv_long = rv_l.reindex(session_dates).to_numpy(dtype=float)
    rv_short = rv_s.reindex(session_dates).to_numpy(dtype=float)

    calm = np.isfinite(ratio) & (ratio < float(p["theta"]))
    calm = calm.astype(float)
    raw = float(p["trend_w"]) * trend + (1.0 - float(p["trend_w"])) * calm
    spike = np.isfinite(spike_ratio) & (spike_ratio > float(p["spike"]))
    w = np.where(spike, 0.0, raw)
    w = np.clip(np.nan_to_num(w, nan=0.0), 0.0, 1.0)
    parts = dict(
        trend=trend,
        calm=calm,
        ratio=ratio,
        spike_ratio=spike_ratio,
        spike=spike.astype(float),
        rv_short=rv_short,
        rv_long=rv_long,
    )
    return w, parts


def _expand_to_bars(ts: pd.DatetimeIndex, w_daily: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Map one target per session to one target per bar.

    The target set at the close of session d is executed at the open of d+1,
    so bars of session d carry w[d-1] and the 15:59 bar carries w[d].
    """
    nd = len(w_daily)
    if nd != len(bt.day_bounds(ts)[1]):
        raise ValueError("session count mismatch")
    if len(ts) == nd:  # already a daily panel
        return np.asarray(w_daily, dtype=float).copy()
    sid = bt.day_ids(ts)
    _, _, last = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    out = np.zeros(len(ts), dtype=float)
    shifted = np.r_[0.0, np.asarray(w_daily, dtype=float)[:-1]]
    out[:] = shifted[sid]
    out[last] = w_daily
    return out


def _check_dev_boundary(ts) -> None:
    """Refuse a panel that extends past the current development end.

    The lead's one-shot holdout runner catches this RuntimeError, sets
    ``END`` to the full-window end and retries.  The signal and weight logic
    are unchanged; this only lets the same code read the holdout daily closes
    when the lead explicitly authorizes it.  A normal development run never
    reaches the raise.
    """
    if len(ts) == 0:
        return
    last = pd.Timestamp(ts[-1])
    if last.tzinfo is None:
        last = last.tz_localize("America/New_York")
    limit = (pd.Timestamp(END, tz="America/New_York").normalize()
             + pd.Timedelta(days=1))
    if last >= limit:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "panel extends past the development window; "
            "the holdout runner may lift END and retry"
        )


def build_weights(ts, o, c, params=None, return_parts=False):
    """Return (n, 3) TQQQ/cash target weights for the harness.

    ``ts`` may be a 1-minute or a daily panel.  The columns of the returned
    matrix follow ``SYMBOLS`` (QQQ, TQQQ, BIL); only TQQQ is used.
    """
    _check_dev_boundary(ts)
    dates, first, _ = bt.day_bounds(ts)
    session_dates = pd.DatetimeIndex(dates[first])
    w_daily, parts = _daily_signals(session_dates, params or {})
    w = _expand_to_bars(ts, w_daily)
    W = np.zeros((len(ts), len(SYMBOLS)), dtype=float)
    W[:, COL_T] = w
    if return_parts:
        return W, w_daily, parts, session_dates
    return W


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# simulation / metrics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _benchmark(ts, c):
    return bt.benchmark(c[:, COL_T], ts, BARS_1M)


def _metrics(ts, o, c, W, cost: float = HEADLINE_COST, start: str = START,
             bars_per_year: float = BARS_1M, end: str | None = None):
    if end is not None:
        j = int(ts.searchsorted(pd.Timestamp(end, tz="America/New_York"), side="right"))
        ts, o, c, W = ts[:j], o[:j], c[:j], W[:j]
    i0 = bt.start_index(ts, start)
    r = bt.run(ts, o, c, W, start, band=BAND, slippage_bps=cost)
    s = bt.stats(r, bars_per_year)
    eq = r["equity"]
    b = c[i0:, COL_T]
    eq_d = bt.daily_last(eq, r["ts"])
    b_d = bt.daily_last(b, r["ts"])
    rets = np.diff(eq_d.to_numpy()) / eq_d.to_numpy()[:-1]
    bret = np.diff(b_d.to_numpy()) / b_d.to_numpy()[:-1]
    corr = float(np.corrcoef(rets, bret)[0, 1]) if len(rets) > 2 else float("nan")
    s["corr_tqqq"] = corr
    s["cagr"] = float(s["cagr"])
    s["max_drawdown"] = float(s["max_drawdown"])
    s["sharpe"] = float(s["sharpe"])
    s["exposure"] = float(s["exposure"])
    s["turnover"] = float(s["turnover"])
    s["fills"] = int(s["fills"])
    return s, r, eq_d, b_d


def _metrics_daily(ts_d, o_d, c_d, W, cost: float = HEADLINE_COST):
    return _metrics(ts_d, o_d, c_d, W, cost=cost, bars_per_year=252)


def _round(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: _round(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        return [_round(v) for v in obj]
    if isinstance(obj, (np.floating, float)):
        return round(float(obj), 6)
    if isinstance(obj, (np.integer, int)):
        return int(obj)
    return obj


def _summary(s):
    return {
        "cagr": s["cagr"],
        "max_drawdown": s["max_drawdown"],
        "sharpe": s["sharpe"],
        "sortino": s.get("sortino"),
        "volatility": s["volatility"],
        "exposure": s.get("exposure"),
        "corr_tqqq": s.get("corr_tqqq"),
        "fills": s.get("fills"),
        "turnover": s.get("turnover"),
        "years": s["years"],
        "ending_equity": s["ending_equity"],
    }


def _yearly(ts, eq, bench):
    return {str(y): {"strategy": v["strategy"], "benchmark": v["benchmark"]}
            for y, v in bt.yearly(ts, eq, bench).items()}


def _yearly_exposure(ts, r):
    eq = r["equity"]
    expo = (eq - r["cash"]) / eq
    out = {}
    for y in sorted(set(ts.year)):
        m = ts.year == y
        out[str(int(y))] = float(np.mean(expo[m]))
    return out


def _binarize(a):
    return (np.asarray(a, dtype=float) > 0.5).astype(float)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# robustness
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _cagr_from_returns(dr: np.ndarray, periods_per_year: float = 252.0) -> float:
    if len(dr) == 0:
        return float("nan")
    return float(np.prod(1.0 + dr) ** (periods_per_year / len(dr)) - 1.0)


def _drop_year_cut(dr: pd.Series, bret: pd.Series, year: int) -> dict:
    keep = dr.index.year != year
    d = dr[keep].to_numpy()
    b = bret[keep].to_numpy()
    return {
        "strategy": _cagr_from_returns(d),
        "benchmark": _cagr_from_returns(b),
        "days": int(len(d)),
    }


def _drop_best_days(dr: pd.Series, bret: pd.Series, n: int = 10) -> dict:
    idx = np.argsort(dr.to_numpy())[-n:]
    d = dr.to_numpy().copy()
    d[idx] = 0.0
    b = bret.to_numpy().copy()
    # also remove the same calendar days from the benchmark for comparability
    b[idx] = 0.0
    return {"strategy": _cagr_from_returns(d), "benchmark": _cagr_from_returns(b),
            "n_days": int(n)}


def _block_shuffle(w: np.ndarray, nd: int, block: int = 20,
                   draws: int = 200, seed: int = 7) -> np.ndarray:
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    out = np.empty((draws, nd), dtype=float)
    for j in range(draws):
        nblocks = int(np.ceil(nd / block))
        starts = rng.integers(0, nd, nblocks)
        idx = np.concatenate([(np.arange(s, s + block) % nd) for s in starts])[:nd]
        out[j] = w[idx]
    return out


def _shift_placebo(parts: dict, params: dict, nd: int, draws: int = 200,
                   seed: int = 11) -> np.ndarray:
    """Circularly shift the term-structure component, keep the trend sleeve."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    trend = parts["trend"]
    calm = parts["calm"]
    spike = _binarize(parts["spike"])
    tw = float(params["trend_w"])
    out = np.empty((draws, nd), dtype=float)
    for j in range(draws):
        k = int(rng.integers(20, nd - 20))
        raw = tw * trend + (1.0 - tw) * np.roll(calm, k)
        out[j] = np.where(np.roll(spike, k) > 0.5, 0.0, raw)
    return np.clip(out, 0.0, 1.0)


def _placebo_stats(ts_d, o_d, c_d, weights, cost=HEADLINE_COST):
    Ws = []
    for w in weights:
        W = np.zeros((len(ts_d), len(SYMBOLS)), dtype=float)
        W[:, COL_T] = np.clip(np.nan_to_num(w, nan=0.0), 0.0, 1.0)
        Ws.append(W)
    results = bt.simulate_many(ts_d, o_d, c_d, Ws, band=BAND,
                               slippage_bps=cost, threads=1)
    return [bt.stats(r, 252) for r in results]


def _pct_rank(dist, value):
    d = np.asarray(dist, dtype=float)
    return float((np.sum(d < value) + 0.5 * np.sum(d == value)) / len(d))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# main
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

    # ---- pre-registered grid ---------------------------------------------
    print("grid ...", flush=True)

        lag_diag[f"lag_{k}"] = _summary(sk)
        print(f"  lag {k}: CAGR {sk['cagr']*100:6.2f}%  DD "
              f"{sk['max_drawdown']*100:5.2f}%  Sharpe {sk['sharpe']:4.2f}", flush=True)

    block_draws = _block_shuffle(w_daily_d, nd_d, block=20, draws=200)
    block_stats = _placebo_stats(ts_d, o_d, c_d, block_draws)
    block_cagr = np.array([s["cagr"] for s in block_stats])
    block_dd = np.array([s["max_drawdown"] for s in block_stats])
    block_sharpe = np.array([s["sharpe"] for s in block_stats])
    block_expo = np.array([s["exposure"] for s in block_stats])

    shift_draws = _shift_placebo(parts_d, PRIMARY, nd_d, draws=200)
    shift_stats = _placebo_stats(ts_d, o_d, c_d, shift_draws)
    shift_cagr = np.array([s["cagr"] for s in shift_stats])
    shift_dd = np.array([s["max_drawdown"] for s in shift_stats])
    shift_sharpe = np.array([s["sharpe"] for s in shift_stats])

    placebo = {
        "block_shuffle_20d": {
            "draws": 200,
            "actual_cagr": float(s_act["cagr"]),
            "actual_dd": float(s_act["max_drawdown"]),
            "actual_sharpe": float(s_act["sharpe"]),
            "actual_exposure": float(s_act["exposure"]),
            "cagr_pct_rank": _pct_rank(block_cagr, s_act["cagr"]),
            "cagr_mean": float(np.mean(block_cagr)),
            "cagr_p05": float(np.percentile(block_cagr, 5)),
            "cagr_p50": float(np.percentile(block_cagr, 50)),
            "cagr_p95": float(np.percentile(block_cagr, 95)),
            "dd_median": float(np.median(block_dd)),
            "sharpe_median": float(np.median(block_sharpe)),
            "exposure_mean": float(np.mean(block_expo)),
        },
        "ts_component_shift": {
            "draws": 200,
            "actual_cagr": float(s_act["cagr"]),
            "cagr_pct_rank": _pct_rank(shift_cagr, s_act["cagr"]),
            "cagr_mean": float(np.mean(shift_cagr)),
            "cagr_p05": float(np.percentile(shift_cagr, 5)),
            "cagr_p50": float(np.percentile(shift_cagr, 50)),
            "cagr_p95": float(np.percentile(shift_cagr, 95)),
            "dd_median": float(np.median(shift_dd)),
            "sharpe_median": float(np.median(shift_sharpe)),
        },
    }
    print(f"  block-shuffle rank {placebo['block_shuffle_20d']['cagr_pct_rank']:.3f}  "
          f"(actual {s_act['cagr']*100:.2f}% vs median "
          f"{np.median(block_cagr)*100:.2f}%)", flush=True)
    print(f"  TS-shift rank      {placebo['ts_component_shift']['cagr_pct_rank']:.3f}  "
          f"(median {np.median(shift_cagr)*100:.2f}%)", flush=True)

    # ---- concentration diagnostics --------------------------------------
    top10 = np.sort(dr.to_numpy())[-10:]
    top10_sum = float(np.sum(np.log1p(top10)))
    total_log = float(np.sum(np.log1p(dr.to_numpy())))
    concentration = {
        "top10_log_share_of_total": top10_sum / total_log if total_log != 0 else None,
        "best_day": float(top10[-1]),
        "worst_day": float(np.min(dr.to_numpy())),
        "positive_day_fraction": float(np.mean(dr.to_numpy() > 0)),
    }

    result = {
        "meta": {
            "slug": "vol-term-structure",
            "window": {"start": START, "end": END},
            "bar": {"cagr": 0.3672, "max_drawdown": 0.8229, "sharpe": 0.82,
                    "source": "lead-provided TQQQ 1-minute-mark development bar"},
            "harness_benchmark": _summary(bench),
            "primary_params": PRIMARY,
            "band": BAND,
            "headline_cost_bp": HEADLINE_COST,
            "costs_bp": list(COSTS),
            "bars_per_year": BARS_1M,
            "grid": [name for name, _ in GRID],
            "notes": "Development window only; no 2024+ data loaded. "
                     "Signals use QQQ adjusted daily closes through the prior "
                     "session close; fills at the next session open.",
        },
        "benchmark": _summary(bench),
        "headline": headline,
        "yearly": yearly,
        "yearly_exposure": yearly_expo,
        "grid": grid,
        "ablations": ablations,
        "simple_rules": simple,
        "bil_idle": bil_idle,
        "subperiods": subperiods,
        "cuts": cuts,
        "placebo": placebo,
        "lag_diagnostic": lag_diag,
        "concentration": concentration,
    }
    result = _round(result)
    out_path = HERE / "result.json"
    with open(out_path, "w") as fh:
        json.dump(result, fh, indent=2, sort_keys=False)
    print(f"wrote {out_path}", flush=True)
    return result
